chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fasting of the Sunnah, so he said: Fasting the three days of every month: Thursday, Wednesday, and Thursday, removes the clots of the heart and the heat of the chest. (He repeated) Thursday, Wednesday, and Thursday. And if he wishes, (he may fast) Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday. And if he wishes, he may fast one day in every ten days, for that is thirty good deeds. And if he wishes to increase, let him increase.

key_terms.بَلَابِلُ الْقَلْبِ: Clots or impurities of the heart
key_terms.وَحَرُ الصَّدْرِ: Heat or burning in the chest

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended days and benefits of voluntary monthly fasting in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Abu Basir to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting the spiritual purification (*tazkiyah*) achieved through consistent voluntary fasting, specifically linking the practice to the removal of 'clots of the heart' (*balabil al-qalb*) and chest heat. The hadith offers flexibility in scheduling—whether fasting three specific days like Wednesday and Thursday, or one day per ten-day cycle—emphasizing that consistency yields thirty good deeds, with the potential for greater reward through increased devotion.
